author: feral-core
description: Author and run multi-step WORKFLOWS for complicated tasks that need several ordered steps. Use this when the user describes a task with multiple stages, e.g. 'first do X, then Y, then save the result', or anything that chains skill calls, web fetches, LLM reasoning, conditions, and notes. Each workflow runs in the background as a resumable TaskFlow. Step types include: skill.invoke (call any skill endpoint), llm.chat (reason / produce text), note.save, memory.search, http.get, sleep, condition (branch), and noop. Steps can reference earlier output via {{previous_output}} and {{step_N}} templating.

endpoints.description: Author and queue a multi-step workflow. Provide a title and an ordered list of steps. Each step is an object with a 'type' and type-specific fields, e.g. {"type":"skill.invoke","skill_id":"web_search","endpoint":"search","args":{"q":"..."}}, {"type":"llm.chat","prompt":"summarize {{previous_output}}"}, {"type":"note.save","content":"{{previous_output}}"}, {"type":"condition","field":"...","op":"truthy","then":3,"else":4}. The workflow runs in the background; poll with get.

params.name: steps
params.description: Ordered list of step objects. Each must have a 'type'. Supported: skill.invoke, llm.chat, note.save, memory.search, http.get, sleep, condition, noop.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Session id to associate the workflow with.

params.name: context
params.description: Optional initial context dict available to step templating.

endpoints.description: List workflows, optionally filtered by session_id and/or status (queued, running, waiting, completed, failed, cancelled).
Get a single workflow by flow_id, including per-step status and results.

params.name: flow_id
params.description: The workflow (flow) id returned by create.

endpoints.description: Cancel a running or queued workflow by flow_id.

Track YOUR OWN task list for the current conversation. Use this for multi-step work you are doing right now: write the complete list when you start, and rewrite it whenever anything changes so the user can see where you are. This is NOT feral_reminders (that is the user's own time-anchored reminders), NOT feral_routines (recurring schedules), NOT the create endpoint above (that queues a workflow the brain executes in the background), and NOT background_task (long-running autonomous runs). Nothing here is executed for you; it is a visible scratchpad. Always send the COMPLETE list, since every call replaces the previous one. Exactly one item may be 'in_progress' at a time, and the call is rejected if more than one is: mark the item you are actually working on now, leave the rest 'pending', and flip finished items to 'completed' rather than deleting them mid-task.

params.name: todos
params.description: The COMPLETE todo list, replacing whatever was stored before. Each item is {"id":"short-stable-id","content":"what to do","status":"pending|in_progress|completed"}. id is optional and is generated when omitted; status defaults to pending. At most 40 items, and at most one may be in_progress.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Session the list belongs to. Leave unset; the runtime fills it from the call context.

endpoints.returns_description: {todos: [{id, content, status}], counts: {pending, in_progress, completed, total}, session_id}

endpoints.description: Instantiate a named first-party workflow pack (template) into a live workflow run.

params.name: workflow_id
params.description: The workflow pack id (from the first-party catalog).

params.name: session_id
params.description: Session id to associate the run with.

params.name: title
params.description: Optional override title for the instantiated run.
